source.title: Persona Non Grata: Single-Method Safety Evaluation Is Incomplete for Persona-Imbued LLMs
source.authors: Wenkai Li; Fan Yang; Shaunak A. Mehta; K. Onoue

page_placements.theme: Steering for unrelated purposes and generic activation perturbations erode refusal

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a refusal direction as a geometric reference for analyzing personality-trait steering, but does not test the claimed refusal-direction intervention. It does not ablate or add the harmful-minus-harmless direction, or measure the effects of doing so on refusal and general capability.
record.gate_note: The study measures cosine alignment between trait-steering vectors and a refusal direction, and reports safety outcomes under persona prompting and trait-vector steering. Those are not direct tests of the claimed refusal-direction ablation or addition. The paper's discussion of multidimensional refusal and harmfulness/refusal separation cites other work; those cited results are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study computes a refusal direction on Llama-3.1-8B and uses it only as a geometric reference for personality-trait CAA vectors. It never ablates or adds that direction, never edits weights, and never runs a jailbreak against it. Its ASR results come from trait-vector steering and persona prompting. The text also does not say how the refusal direction was derived.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that single-method persona safety evaluation is incomplete and that vulnerability profiles depend on method and architecture. They call trait-refusal alignment a partial, Llama-specific geometric account, and say reasoning gives only graded protection. They make no causal claim about the refusal direction itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts CAA vectors from high-versus-low personality-trait sentence pairs and adds them at selected layers; it does not derive the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction and ablate or add that direction. It reports persona safety outcomes and geometric alignments rather than the claimed refusal-direction intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Persona safety outcomes vary with imbuing method, model architecture, persona, domain, and steering coefficient. The study reports that coefficient affects ASR and that persona rankings can invert between prompting and activation steering.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama-3.1-8B, single-trait AS ASR is predicted by the trait vector's cosine with the refusal direction (R²=0.667, p=0.004; Fig. 2b). Conscientiousness is most anti-aligned (−0.164) and neuroticism is the only positively aligned trait (+0.079).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering vectors for unrelated concepts that are anti-aligned with the refusal direction raise unsafe-response rates, roughly in proportion to their anti-alignment (correlational, one model).

fits_no_version.finding: The Qwen3.5-9B trait-refusal alignment sign pattern matches Llama on all 5 traits (ρ=0.80, p=0.104, not significant).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trait-refusal alignment patterns may be shared across architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Persona safety outcomes differ by imbuing method and architecture. The P12 prosocial persona is safe under prompting (0.038) but unsafe under trait steering (0.818).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety under persona imbuing depends on whether it is done by prompt or by activation steering.

record.problems: The paper describes its trait-refusal alignment account as partial and model-specific, and notes that cross-architecture validation is incomplete. The cross-method comparison is not a fully factorized causal comparison. Some reasoning diagnostics are explicitly heuristic and exploratory. No general-capability evaluation accompanies the safety outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: the full per-persona and per-domain ASR tables (Appendix E and Tables 10–12) and coefficient-ablation condition table (Appendix M/Table 24). They concern trait-vector persona steering rather than an intervention on the refusal direction; the aggregate method results and the directly relevant P12 matched-strength comparison are retained.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the harmful-minus-harmless direction. No measure of refusal removal or induction, or of retained capability.

No jailbreak attack is analysed for suppression of the direction, and there is no adversarial training against ablation. The trait-alignment vs. AS-ASR correlation concerns persona steering vectors, not jailbreaks.
Multi-dimensional refusal is only cited (Pan et al., Wollschläger et al.), not tested.
Harm/refusal separation is only cited (Zhao et al.), not tested.
No transfer of the refusal direction across languages, variants or base/instruct. The Qwen3.5-9B sign match concerns trait-refusal alignment patterns.
No comparison of training methods or stages.
Reasoning models get only persona prompting and trait steering. No refusal-direction intervention.

missing.what: Regression of single-trait AS ASR on trait-refusal cosine alignment (R²=0.667, p=0.004); the closest result to a refusal-direction mechanism, recorded under fits_no_version, bears on no version
Refusal direction norm by layer (2.5 at L8 to 7.7 at L24) on Llama-3.1-8B

record.verdict_notes: Correlational use of the refusal direction only. How the direction was derived (dataset, layer, method) is not stated in the text. All rows correctly link to none.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction is ablated or added; no test of whether removing it eliminates refusals, induces harmless-request refusals, or preserves general capability.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
No test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
The paper cites work on richer refusal geometry but does not itself test whether refusal is affine, conical, or distributed across multiple directions.
No experiment separates harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Cross-model trait/refusal alignment is reported, but the study does not test transfer of the claimed refusal direction across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages for whether a removable refusal direction exists.
Reasoning models are evaluated under persona prompting and trait-vector steering, not under ablation or addition of the claimed refusal direction.

relation.reason: It computes a Llama-3.1-8B refusal direction and uses it to explain persona-steering ASR. It runs no intervention on the direction itself.

tranche.reason: The refusal direction serves only as a fixed geometric reference for cosine comparisons with the trait CAA vectors. The study never ablates, adds or weight-edits that direction, so none of V1–V8 is tested. The cosine-to-ASR correlation over about 10 single-trait personas is a correlational account of trait steering, not a test of the direction's causal role.

source_check.notes: The text never says how its refusal direction was computed: no harmful/harmless sets and no difference-in-means are described. So the record's recipe line ('does not derive the harmful-minus-harmless direction') should say the derivation is not stated. The cosine framework is Llama-only, and the authors call it partial. They report only sign consistency on Qwen3.5-9B, with no numbers.

statements.problem: Numbers are correct. R2=0.667 and p=0.004 appear only as an annotation on the Figure 2b panel (single-trait AS ASR against trait-refusal cosine, Llama-3.1-8B). -0.164 is Table 14's mean over layers 8–24.
